_meta.note: Static sections (groups, fixtures) never change manually. To refresh, open Claude Code in this repo and say: 'Search for all completed 2026 World Cup results and update the results, standings and _meta.last_updated in scores.json, then commit and push.' Claude should only update the results, standings and _meta sections — never touch fixtures or groups.

funnies.headline: 44 years after the 'Disgrace of Gijón', Algeria and Austria played out their own 3-3 draw to advance together — and the internet erupted
funnies.summary: In 1982 in Spain, West Germany and Austria played a collusive 1-0 draw they both needed to eliminate Algeria from the World Cup. It became known as the 'Disgrace of Gijón' and scarred Algeria for a generation. On Sunday in Kansas City, Algeria played Austria in their Group J finale — both needing only a draw to advance at Iran's expense. What followed was anything but collusive: a pulsating 3-3 thriller in which Riyad Mahrez scored with barely a minute of stoppage time remaining to seemingly seal Algeria's progress, before Sasa Kalajdzic immediately equalised at the other end to make it 3-3. Both nations advanced. Iran — watching at home — were eliminated. The internet found the 1982 footage within minutes. 'This time,' wrote one Algerian journalist, 'we were IN on it.'

funnies.headline: DR Congo win a World Cup match for the first time ever — three goals in 22 minutes against Uzbekistan sends them through
funnies.summary: DR Congo, playing in only their second ever World Cup, had never won a match at the tournament in any of their appearances. That changed in Atlanta on Sunday. Yoane Wissa converted a penalty on 68 minutes to equalise after Eldor Shomurodov's early opener, Fiston Mayele made it 2-1 on 78, and Wissa struck again in stoppage time to seal a 3-1 win. DR Congo reach the Round of 32 for the first time in their history. Back in Kinshasa, fans flooded the streets. Statue superfan Michel Mboladinga — who had stood perfectly still through the Colombia game — was photographed dancing. The statue was finally alive.

funnies.headline: Davinson Sánchez headed Colombia into the lead in stoppage time against Portugal — then VAR ruled it offside by millimetres
funnies.summary: Colombia had 24 shots, dominated possession, and created chance after chance against a Portugal side happy to sit on a 0-0 and go through as group runners-up. Then, deep into stoppage time, Davinson Sánchez powered a header into the net. The Colombian bench erupted. Players sprinted the length of the pitch. Then came the VAR check. By the tiniest of margins, Sánchez had been fractionally offside at the moment of the cross. The goal was disallowed. The game ended 0-0. Colombia, who still won Group K with 7 points, went from celebrating a perfect group stage to being denied a piece of history by a system of millimetres.

funnies.headline: Luka Modrić, 40 years old and on his 201st cap, became the oldest player in World Cup history to register an assist
funnies.summary: Croatia needed a result against Ghana to reach the Round of 32, and their captain delivered. In the 83rd minute, with the score at 1-1 and Croatia on the verge of elimination, Luka Modrić — 40 years, 11 months old and winning his 201st international cap — rolled a pass into Nikola Vlasic, who smashed home the winner. The assist made Modrić the oldest player ever to record a World Cup assist, breaking a record that had stood for decades. Croatia advance to face Portugal. Modrić, who nearly retired from international football two years ago, was mobbed by teammates. 'He could play until he's 50,' said Vlasic.

funnies.headline: Iran's Khalilzadeh thought he'd sent his country to the knockouts — then VAR crushed them in the 93rd minute
funnies.summary: With Egypt and Iran locked at 1-1 in their decisive Group G clash at Lumen Field in Seattle, Iran defender Shoja Khalilzadeh rifled into the roof of the net in the 93rd minute. The Iranian bench erupted, players sprinted across the pitch to celebrate, and the packed away end lost its mind. Then came the VAR check. Two Iranian attackers had drifted into offside positions at the critical moment of a flick-on deep in the area, and after an agonising wait, the goal was chalked off. Final score: 1-1. Egypt advance to the R32 as Group G runners-up; Iran — three points, zero goals conceded in extra time — must wait in desperate hope of being one of the eight best third-placed teams. Khalilzadeh was still sitting on the pitch, head in hands, long after the final whistle.

funnies.headline: Cape Verde reach the World Cup R32 without winning a single match — three draws, zero victories, history made
funnies.summary: Cape Verde's World Cup debut will go down in football history — for all the right reasons. In their first-ever World Cup, the Blue Sharks drew all three group games (0-0 vs Spain, 2-2 vs Uruguay, 0-0 vs Saudi Arabia) and never won once. Yet three draws and three points were enough to advance as runners-up from Group H, ahead of both Uruguay and Saudi Arabia on goal difference. They become the first team in World Cup history to reach the knockout stage without recording a single group-stage victory. They face Argentina in Miami in the Round of 32. Goalkeeper Vozinha, now with over 3 million Instagram followers, is fresh and fully rested.

funnies.headline: Egypt and Iran formally object to FIFA over 'Pride Match' branding in Seattle — Iran demands ban on rainbow flags inside stadium
funnies.summary: As Egypt and Iran prepared for their Group G finale at Lumen Field in Seattle, organisers branded the fixture a 'Pride Match' to coincide with LGBTQ Pride celebrations in the city. Both nations — where homosexuality is illegal — formally objected to FIFA. Iran's Football Federation President called it 'an irrational move that supports a certain group' and demanded all pride flags be banned inside the stadium. FIFA declined to intervene. It became one of the most diplomatically fraught incidents of the entire tournament, drawing statements from multiple governments and human rights organisations.

funnies.headline: Dembélé scores the second-fastest hat-trick in World Cup history — all three in 32 minutes as France thrash Norway 4-1
funnies.summary: With coach Didier Deschamps absent to attend his mother's funeral, France needed a response — and got one from an unlikely hero. Ousmane Dembélé, starting in place of the rested Kylian Mbappé, scored three times in the first 32 minutes against Norway at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough. Only Austria's Erich Probst (24 minutes, 1954) has scored a World Cup hat-trick faster. Désiré Doué added a fourth late on. It was only the third hat-trick ever scored by a French player at a World Cup. Norway — who had topped the group going into the game — ended up second, with Haaland left on the bench throughout.

funnies.headline: Didier Deschamps misses France's final group game to fly home to France for his mother's funeral
funnies.summary: France head coach Didier Deschamps, who announced before the tournament that this would be his final World Cup in charge after 14 years, was dealt a devastating personal blow mid-tournament when his mother passed away. He flew back to France to attend her funeral, leaving assistant Guy Stéphan to take charge of the decisive Group I clash against Norway — a match that would decide who topped the group. Both teams had already qualified for the knockouts. 'We are all behind him at this incredibly difficult time,' said captain Mbappé. Deschamps, 57, planned to return to the squad after the ceremony.

funnies.headline: Türkiye stun USA 3-2 with a 98th-minute winner — USA had made nine changes and still didn't have enough
funnies.summary: The United States, already guaranteed to top Group D, made nine changes for their final group game against Türkiye at Los Angeles Stadium. Auston Trusty put USA ahead in the 3rd minute. Arda Güler equalised in the 10th, Orkun Kökcü made it 2-1, then Sebastian Berhalter's rocket from outside the box restored parity at 2-2 (49'). Then, in the 8th minute of stoppage time, Güler nutmegged Christian Pulisic, Can Uzun's cross squeezed through Matt Turner's legs and past three defenders, and substitute Kaan Ayhan poked it home. Turkey, already eliminated, had nothing to play for — and celebrated as if they'd won the tournament. USA still topped the group.

funnies.headline: New Zealand's Tyler Bindon and his mum Jenny become the first mother-and-son pair to play at separate World Cups
funnies.summary: When Tyler Bindon came off the bench in the 92nd minute of New Zealand's 2-2 draw with Iran at SoFi Stadium, he completed a piece of history no son had made before. His mother Jenny Bindon is a New Zealand international goalkeeper who played at the Women's World Cups of 2007 and 2011. With Tyler's appearance, they became the first mother-son pair in World Cup history across men's and women's tournaments. Tyler plays for Nottingham Forest. He was partly raised by the Football Ferns squad when the family relocated to California for Jenny's coaching role at UCLA. Jenny watched from the stands. FIFA called it 'a uniquely beautiful moment in World Cup history'.

funnies.headline: Ecuador stun Germany 2-1 to reach the knockouts — Germany had already won the group and were 'resting'
funnies.summary: Germany had already secured top spot in Group E and made changes ahead of the knockouts. Ecuador, needing a win to survive as a best third-place team, took full advantage. Leroy Sané put Germany ahead in the 2nd minute; Nilson Angulo levelled in the 9th; then Gonzalo Plata headed home a corner in the 77th to send MetLife Stadium into pandemonium. Ecuador reach the Round of 32 for the first time since 2006. Germany finish second in the group on goal difference despite the defeat — but it's their first group-stage loss since 2018.

funnies.headline: Ivory Coast reach a World Cup Round of 32 for the very FIRST TIME — four World Cup attempts, four group exits, until now
funnies.summary: In four previous World Cup appearances (2006, 2010, 2014, 2023) Ivory Coast had never made it past the group stage. That ended on Thursday night in Philadelphia. Nicolas Pépé scored a brace in a 2-0 win over Curaçao to seal their historic first knockout-stage qualification. Ivory Coast finish second in Group E on goal difference behind Germany. Their Round of 32 opponents: Norway, group winners from Group I.

funnies.headline: South Africa reach World Cup knockouts for the FIRST TIME EVER — coach Broos collapsed to the turf at full-time
funnies.summary: Thapelo Maseko's 63rd-minute counter-attack goal against South Korea sent the Bafana Bafana to a World Cup Round of 32 for the very first time — a feat they never achieved even when hosting in 2010. Coach Hugo Broos, 72, sank to his knees and then to the ground at the final whistle as his substitutes piled on top of him. South Africa had been widely written off after losing 2-0 to Mexico on day one; they rallied with a draw vs Czechia, then won the match that mattered most. They face Canada in Los Angeles in the R32.

funnies.headline: Bosnia's 18-year-old Alajbegović scores the early contender for Goal of the Tournament — then eliminates Qatar
funnies.summary: Kerim Alajbegović — 18 years old, playing in his first World Cup — opened the scoring against Qatar with a long-range curler that the highlight team titled 'Goal of the Tournament'. He ran the length of the pitch, received the ball, and bent it into the top corner from 25 yards. Bosnia won 3-1 to eliminate Qatar and keep their own knockout hopes alive. 'He has no fear,' said coach Sergej Barbarez. 'He plays like he's been in five World Cups already.'

funnies.headline: Alisson makes two stunning late saves to deny Scotland — but Vinicius Jr and Selecão top Group C in style
funnies.summary: Vinicius Júnior scored twice (7', 45+2') and Matheus Cunha added a third (60') as Brazil strolled past Scotland 3-0. But Scotland pushed hard in the final 20 minutes, forcing Alisson Becker into superb saves to deny Scott McTominay and Lewis Ferguson from close range. Scotland end with 3 points in third place and must wait to learn if they're among the eight best third-placed teams to make the knockouts — their -3 goal difference makes it uncertain.

funnies.headline: DR Congo superfan Michel Mboladinga stood completely still for 90 minutes as a Patrice Lumumba statue — after missing their opener due to Ebola quarantine
funnies.summary: Michel Mboladinga, Congo DR's famous 'statue fan', went viral during the Africa Cup of Nations for standing perfectly motionless throughout entire matches, arms raised, posing as a memorial statue of the country's assassinated first prime minister Patrice Lumumba. He'd missed DR Congo's World Cup opener against Portugal because Ebola quarantine requirements meant he couldn't enter the United States in time. He finally made it for the Colombia match in Guadalajara, took his place in the stands, and stood completely still for 90 minutes as Colombia won 1-0. The internet erupted: clips of him surrounded by dancing fans cut with shots of the statue itself became the most-shared image of the week.

funnies.headline: 8,000 Scotland fans took over a Miami Marlins game, Billy Gilmour threw out the first pitch, and bagpipers marched around the warning track
funnies.summary: With Scotland facing Brazil in Miami on Wednesday, the Tartan Army arrived two days early and needed something to do. Solution: buy 8,000 tickets to the Miami Marlins vs Texas Rangers game at loanDepot Park. Injured Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour threw out the first pitch. Fans in full kilts danced in the aisles to 'Yes Sir, I Can Boogie'. Bagpipers led a march around the warning track. When a kid in an Argentina jersey was spotted, the entire section erupted in Maradona chants. The Marlins PA staff played traditional Scottish folk music between innings. The game sold out almost entirely in Tartan Army tartan. It's been called the most unexpected crossover event of the 2026 World Cup.

funnies.headline: Germany lose Nico Schlotterbeck for the rest of the World Cup — he's choosing to stay with the squad anyway
funnies.summary: Nico Schlotterbeck went down in the first half of Germany's 2-1 win over Ivory Coast but played on through half-time before being replaced by Antonio Rüdiger. An MRI confirmed a torn medial ligament in his left ankle — minimum two months out, ruling him out of the entire knockout stage. It was described as a 'devastating blow' by the German FA. What caught the world's attention was what came next: Schlotterbeck announced he would remain with the squad at their North Carolina base to support his teammates rather than fly home. The DFB confirmed no replacement would be called up. Several Germany players posted tributes. Joshua Kimmich, who'd already warned the squad about venomous snakes, called Schlotterbeck's decision 'the most German thing I've ever seen'.

funnies.headline: Ronaldo scores in his SIXTH World Cup at 41 — the first player in history, men's or women's, to do so
funnies.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41 years and 138 days old, opened the scoring in the 6th minute of Portugal's 5-0 thrashing of Uzbekistan to become the first player in World Cup history — across men's and women's football — to score in six different tournaments. He added a second in the second half. His 10 World Cup goals are now a Portugal record, and at 41 he is the second-oldest scorer in World Cup history behind Cameroon's Roger Milla (42 in 1994). Before the match he'd been the subject of widespread criticism for his performance against DR Congo. He answered in typically understated fashion.

funnies.headline: Harry Kane somehow blasts an empty net over the crossbar in the 86th minute — England held 0-0 by Ghana
funnies.summary: England controlled the ball for 60% of the match and created 3.0 xG against a Ghana side ranked 65th in the world, yet couldn't score. The crowning moment of frustration came in the 86th minute: Nico O'Reilly's header struck the crossbar and bounced back to Harry Kane, England's all-time top scorer, six yards out with the goal gaping. Kane somehow blasted it high and wide. He held his head in his hands; the Boston crowd did likewise. England stay top of Group L on goal difference from Ghana, but the result means their round-of-32 place still isn't mathematically sealed.

funnies.headline: Algeria come from behind to eliminate World Cup debutants Jordan 2-1 — a comeback the Fennec Foxes have NEVER managed at a World Cup before
funnies.summary: Jordan had given their fans in Amman something to dream about when Moussa Al-Rashdan headed them in front on 36 minutes — a lead that stood deep into the second half. But Algeria, needing a win to progress, conjured a comeback for the ages. Riyad Mahrez swung in a corner and Benbouali glanced it home (69'); then, with eight minutes left, Amine Gouiri poked in the winner (82') — VAR checked it and confirmed. According to FIFA records, Algeria had never previously come from behind to win in all 10 World Cup matches where they conceded first. Jordan depart the tournament with their heads held high after a historic debut.

funnies.headline: Doku flies home to welcome son Praise — then French TV host says 'the dad is useless' and the internet erupts
funnies.summary: Belgium winger Jérémy Doku missed the squad's 0-0 draw with Iran and flew to London to be present for the birth of his first child. It seemed like a lovely story. Then French TV presenter France Pierron went on air and described childbirth as 'a disgusting moment, excuse me, where the dad is useless.' The backlash was instant and global. Belgian teammates, global football figures and parents around the world reacted with fury. Pierron issued a grovelling apology within 48 hours: 'I understand that they may have shocked, offended, or hurt some of you, and I am sorry for that.' Doku's son, Praise, was born on Monday. Doku returned to the squad in time to see Belgium beat New Zealand 5-1.

funnies.headline: France vs Iraq was suspended for 28 minutes by a lightning storm — Mbappé had just scored to make it 1-0
funnies.summary: Kylian Mbappé had barely finished celebrating his opening goal at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia when storm clouds rolled in, lightning struck near the stadium, and officials pulled the players off. The 28-minute delay saw fans sheltering under every overhang in the building and the BBC commentator wondering aloud if the match would be completed. It was: France returned to the pitch and scored twice more to win 3-0, Mbappé adding his second. Iraq, who arrived knowing they were already eliminated, at least got the most theatrical exit in the tournament.

funnies.headline: 100-year-old Messi superfan shows up to Argentina vs Austria — with a marriage proposal sign
funnies.summary: Pauline Kana, a 100-year-old American and Guinness World Record holder for crowd surfing, travelled to Dallas to watch Argentina play Austria and held up a sign reading '100-Year-Old Messi Fan' in the stands — then produced a second sign proposing marriage to Lionel Messi. When her face appeared on the big screen, the stadium roared. The centenarian, who creates viral content with her grandson Ross Smith, has attended multiple Messi matches over the years. She was in the building as Messi broke the all-time men's World Cup scoring record with two goals. Afterwards she told reporters she was still waiting for Messi's answer: 'I've been patient this long.'

funnies.headline: Messi scores twice against Austria to become the men's World Cup's all-time leading goalscorer with 18 — and he's still only playing in the group stage
funnies.summary: In Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria in Dallas, Lionel Messi — 38 years old, playing in his sixth World Cup — scored both goals to move to 18 career World Cup strikes, two clear of Miroslav Klose's previous record. His first goal levelled the record at 17; his second, with Messi in tears before full-time, broke it. He now has five goals in two games at this tournament alone. Several sitting heads of state posted tributes. His Argentina teammates formed a guard of honour at the whistle. The word 'GOAT', again, crashed the internet.

funnies.headline: King and Queen of the Netherlands gatecrashed two World Cup dressing rooms in one night — and Eloy Room kissed the Queen
funnies.summary: After the Netherlands beat Sweden 5-1 and Ecuador drew 0-0 with Curaçao on the same night, King Willem-Alexander and Queen Máxima of the Netherlands managed the remarkable feat of joining both dressing rooms in sequence. First they congratulated the Dutch squad, then they surprised the Curaçao players — who had just earned their first-ever World Cup point, thanks to goalkeeper Eloy Room's extraordinary 15 saves. The squad were stunned to find royalty walking through the door. Room — who later said 'We danced in the locker room, it was just wonderful' — was photographed giving Queen Máxima a kiss. The images went viral and briefly made Curaçao the most talked-about team in the tournament.

funnies.headline: Lamine Yamal becomes one of the youngest WC scorers ever as Spain dismantle Saudi Arabia 4-0
funnies.summary: After their tense 0-0 draw with Cape Verde, Spain needed a reaction — and got one with interest. Lamine Yamal, 18, opened the scoring in the 10th minute with his first ever World Cup goal, making him one of the youngest scorers in the tournament's history, eclipsing records set by Messi, Mbappé and Ronaldo. Mikel Oyarzabal added two more inside 25 minutes, and an own goal from Hassan Al-Tambakti sealed a 4-0 rout. Saudi Arabia — who famously upset Argentina in 2022 — were thoroughly outclassed. Spain sealed their Round of 32 spot and top Group H.

funnies.headline: Paraguay's Almirón becomes first player ever red-carded at a World Cup for covering his mouth
funnies.summary: Almirón had just helped Paraguay go 1-0 up against Türkiye when he was spotted covering his mouth while apparently exchanging words with a Turkish defender. VAR intervened. Straight red. Almirón broke down in tears on the touchline. Why? FIFA's new 'Prestianni Law' makes it an instant dismissal to deliberately hide your lips during an altercation — a rule introduced after a Chilean player used the trick to racially abuse Vinícius Júnior in the Champions League. Paraguay held on to win with ten men. The rule is now more famous than the match.

funnies.headline: Norway's 'Viking Row' conquered Boston escalators, Times Square — then the Norwegian parliament joined in
funnies.summary: Norway fans have a tradition: the 'Viking Row' — arms locked, rowing in unison like longship oarsmen, roaring 'Ro! Ro! Ro!'. It went viral when a full escalator at Boston's South Station did it perfectly synchronised on the way to the Iraq match. Then Norway fans took over Times Square. Then, on Thursday, Norwegian MPs performed it on the floor of the Storting (parliament) in solidarity. The team is unbeaten and top of Group I. The escalator video has 40 million views.

funnies.headline: Canada beat Qatar 6-0 in their first ever World Cup win — 40 years after their only previous appearance
funnies.summary: Canada had never won a World Cup match in their history — not in 1986, not in 2022. On Thursday they beat Qatar 6-0, with Jonathan David bagging a hat-trick. Canadian fans sang O Canada for what felt like an hour. One viral tweet: 'Canada waited 40 years for their first World Cup win and immediately went absolutely feral.' The players were seen doing the griddy on the pitch.

funnies.headline: Messi scores his first ever World Cup hat-trick — on his 200th cap, in his 6th World Cup, to equal Klose's all-time goals record
funnies.summary: Argentina beat Algeria 3-0, but the scoreline barely mattered. At 38 years old, Messi scored all three goals to reach 16 World Cup goals — level with Miroslav Klose's all-time record. It was his 200th cap for Argentina, his 6th World Cup appearance (a men's record), and his first hat-trick at the tournament. Patrick Mahomes, Rio Ferdinand and roughly the entire internet lost their minds.

funnies.headline: England fans dressed as cowboys, attempted calf roping and sang 'Sweet Caroline' at a Fort Worth rodeo before the Croatia game
funnies.summary: With England's opener in Dallas, fans descended on the Fort Worth Stockyards the day before — swapping pints for Stetsons. Videos went viral of Three Lions supporters in full cowboy hats attempting barrel racing, doing line dancing and belting out Sweet Caroline to a very confused rodeo crowd. NBC 5 Dallas called it 'the most English thing ever done in Texas'.

funnies.headline: While Messi scored a hat-trick, 41-year-old Ronaldo became the oldest outfield player ever to start a World Cup match
funnies.summary: On the same evening, Cristiano Ronaldo became the oldest outfield player to ever start a World Cup game, aged 41, as Portugal drew 1-1 with DR Congo. He didn't score. Messi scored three. The 'GOAT debate' ran so hot on social media that 'Ronaldo' was trending alongside 'Klose record', 'Messi GOAT', and — inevitably — 'retirement'.

funnies.headline: Sprinkler malfunction soaks Gillette Stadium pitch at halftime of Iraq vs Norway — staff deployed buckets
funnies.summary: At halftime of Iraq v Norway at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, a sprinkler head malfunctioned on the edge of the penalty area, sending a large jet of water across the pitch for several seconds. Groundskeepers sprinted on with buckets and tools to disperse the flood; the rest of the sprinkler system had to be shut down entirely to stop the damage spreading. The pitch was back to normal by kick-off of the second half — which was just as well, as Norway ran riot in it to win 4-1.

funnies.headline: Joshua Kimmich warns Germany squad of venomous snake at their training base: 'I don't think you'll die, but it's certainly dangerous'
funnies.summary: Germany are based in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and Joshua Kimmich held a press conference to update journalists on the squad's wellbeing. The headline: a copperhead snake — one of North America's most venomous species — had been spotted near the training pitch. 'We were told if you get bitten, you have to go to hospital,' said Kimmich. 'I don't think you'll die, but it's certainly dangerous.' Days earlier they beat Curaçao 7-1.

funnies.headline: Cape Verde's 40-year-old goalkeeper gains 3 million Instagram followers overnight after stunning Spain
funnies.summary: Vozinha had 20,000 followers when the match kicked off. By full-time — after making seven saves to hold Spain to a 0-0 draw in Cape Verde's first ever World Cup match — he had over 3 million. He then broke down in tears as teammates mobbed him. Only one 'keeper aged 40+ has made more saves in a single World Cup game since 1966 (Pat Jennings, 1986).

funnies.headline: German fan Freddy discovers America one chain restaurant at a time and takes 600,000 followers with him
funnies.summary: Freddy arrived in New York with 11,000 followers on a tight budget and a plan to drive across the country to games. Taco Bell was 'the holy land', a Waffle House visit earned a glowing review, and Buc-ee's left him lost for words. By June 15 he had 600,000 followers along for the ride. Republicans began citing him as proof the US was 'fun again'.

funnies.headline: Lawrence, Kansas fell completely in love with Algeria — Riyad Mahrez kicked a field goal and the town chanted 'Rock Chalk Algeria'
funnies.summary: Algeria's World Cup base camp is the University of Kansas in Lawrence. KU's football team invited the squad onto the pitch; Riyad Mahrez put on a helmet and booted a field goal clean through the uprights. It went massively viral. Hundreds of locals turned up for open training sessions, children wore Algerian face paint, the Marching Jayhawks band played Algeria's national anthem, and 'Rock Chalk Algeria' — a riff on the university's famous 'Rock Chalk Jayhawk' chant — spread across social media. It's been called the most wholesome subplot of the tournament.

funnies.headline: USMNT goalkeeper Matt Turner throws a perfect strike at LA Angels game — then meets Mike Trout
funnies.summary: On a day off from World Cup preparations, US goalkeeper Matt Turner threw out the ceremonial first pitch at an LA Angels vs Tampa Bay Rays game. Turner delivered a clean strike straight into the catcher's mitt. 'The highlight of the day was throwing a perfect strike,' he said, adding that catcher Logan O'Hoppe was complimentary. He also got to meet Mike Trout: 'To get to meet one of the best to ever do it — that was something special.' He then kept a clean sheet as the USA beat Australia 2-0 four days later.

funnies.headline: German fan cycled 26,000km through 27 countries over 21 months to reach Houston for Germany's opener
funnies.summary: Jakob Alberti, 26, from Karlsruhe set off on his bike nearly two years before the World Cup with one goal: make it to Houston for Germany's first game. His route took him through Austria, the Balkans, Türkiye, the UAE, India, Thailand, Australia and 27 countries in total — and he ran a marathon in every country he visited. He arrived at NRG Stadium just in time to watch Germany beat Curaçao 7-1. FIFA profiled him and the story went enormously viral. His plan after the tournament: cycle home via North Africa.

funnies.headline: Scotland fans export their finest tradition to Boston — orange traffic cones on every statue they can find
funnies.summary: In Glasgow, it's the Duke of Wellington. In Boston, it's anyone who'll stand still. Tartan Army fans have been spotted placing traffic cones on historic statues across the city, prompting locals to start calling Boston 'New Scotland'. Social media lit up with comparisons — and one tweet noting that the city was 'already used to drunk fans in kilts, so it's basically Edinburgh anyway'.

funnies.headline: NZ defender goes from 'least known player at the World Cup' to 1.5 million Instagram followers overnight
funnies.summary: Argentine content creator Valen Scarsini posted a video identifying New Zealand's Tim Payne — who had fewer followers than his own national team's account — as the tournament's most obscure player. He asked fans to follow him. By the next morning Payne had 1.5 million followers, fan accounts, custom shirts and a nickname: 'El Timmy'.

funnies.headline: NFL quarterback Jameis Winston helped Japan fans clean the stadium — then the internet argued about whether he meant it
funnies.summary: After Japan's dramatic 2-2 draw with the Netherlands in Dallas, FOX Sports correspondent Jameis Winston joined Japanese fans in their famous post-match rubbish collection, carrying a blue bin bag around the stands. FOX broadcast it live. Within hours, critics were saying it was a PR stunt for the cameras. His former teammate Alvin Kamara then posted: 'He really is just a genuinely good dude in real life… cameras or not.' Mahomes agreed. The debate got nearly as much attention as the match itself.

funnies.headline: Haaland waved a Carolina Hurricanes towel at the Stanley Cup Final, then scored twice in his World Cup debut three days later
funnies.summary: With Norway's opener still days away, Erling Haaland and several teammates headed to Raleigh for Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Finals. When the camera found him on the big screen, he waved a Hurricanes rally towel with the enthusiasm of a lifelong season-ticket holder. The NHL immediately posted: 'Confirmed: Erling Haaland is now a huge Carolina Hurricanes fan.' He then scored twice against Iraq in Boston. The Canes lost the Cup anyway.

funnies.headline: Scotland fan plays bagpipes outside Boston Airbnb at 6:30am — neighbour films it, 9 million views follow
funnies.summary: Local resident Mike Morrison was woken by a lone piper in full regalia serenading the street before the Haiti v Scotland game. He filmed it, posted it, and by the afternoon had 9 million views. By the evening the Tartan Army had invited him over for drinks. He ended the night writing 'Viva #Scotland'.

funnies.headline: Peruvian police disguise themselves as 2026 World Cup mascots to bust a drug dealer
funnies.summary: Officers from Peru's anti-narcotics unit dressed as Clutch the Bald Eagle and Maple the Moose — the official FIFA 2026 mascots — to ambush a drug dealer they described as a 'diehard football fan', reasoning he might open the door for mascots where he wouldn't for police. They broke through a gate with a battering ram, arrested 48-year-old Carlos Cabrera, and seized 2,524 packets of cocaine base and a firearm. Footage of the costumed officers making the bust went viral within hours. It reportedly wasn't Peru's first creative disguise operation: on Valentine's Day 2025, an officer dressed as a capybara made a drugs arrest.

funnies.headline: Thomas Partey denied entry to Canada, misses Ghana's opener
funnies.summary: Ghana's captain was refused entry by Canadian border officials and couldn't travel from the team's Rhode Island base to Toronto for their opener against Panama. The irony: he'd have been fine for their next match in the US. FIFA stressed it has no say in host nations' immigration decisions.

funnies.headline: The Brazilian referee explained his red card decision in English — nobody had any idea what he said
funnies.summary: FIFA's new 'referee mic' initiative produced its first viral moment when Brazilian official Wilton Sampaio announced a red card decision over the stadium PA in English during Mexico v South Africa. Players, staff and fans alike looked completely baffled. Screenshots of South Africa's Khuliso Mudau's bewildered expression spread instantly — the first meme of the 2026 World Cup.

funnies.headline: FIFA blames empty seats at South Korea match on fans watching from the concourse
funnies.summary: Sections of the Guadalajara stadium looked worryingly empty during South Korea v Czechia — until FIFA explained that thousands of ticketed fans had simply decided they'd rather watch from the concourse and hang around the concession stands.

funnies.headline: England arrive in Kansas City to find boots, balls and kit stolen from team van
funnies.summary: Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and co. were left with just one training ball after thieves broke into the squad's transit vehicles. Players' custom match boots and official World Cup balls were among the haul. Two suspects have since been arrested.

funnies.headline: Merlín the duck, dressed in a tiny Mexico jersey and custom duck socks, went viral as Mexico City erupted
funnies.summary: After Mexico's 2-0 win over South Africa on opening night, street vendor Carla Gómez led her pet duck Merlín — wearing a miniature Mexico shirt and bespoke duck socks — through the celebrating crowds on Reforma Avenue. The footage racked up millions of views within hours. Calls for Merlín to replace the official mascot (Zayu the jaguar) spread across Spanish-language social media. The official mascot has not responded.

funnies.headline: FOX Sports ran so many ads during the World Cup hydration break it missed the restart
funnies.summary: During the very first match of the tournament, FOX cut to commercial during the cooling break — and ran so many ads that viewers were still watching Powerade spots when Mexico kicked off again. FIFA rules say broadcasters must be back on air 30 seconds before play resumes.

funnies.headline: Scotland fans' US travel permits revoked days before their first World Cup in 28 years
funnies.summary: Dozens of Tartan Army fans had their ESTAs flipped to 'Travel Not Authorized' with no explanation just days before flying out, threatening to miss Scotland's first World Cup since 1998. Scotland's First Minister vowed to 'do all I can to help'. One fan said Trump should 'return the hospitality'.
